subject: Private hosting interface matrix request
messages:
From: Nina Rao <nina.rao@medicore.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com
Cc: security@medicore.com
Date: 2025-04-11T09:12:00Z
Subject: Private hosting interface matrix request

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking the time on the call earlier. As a follow-up, our security team asked if you can provide a concise 'Private Hosting Interface Matrix' that covers the following for Redwood's private/VPC deployments in APAC:

- Network endpoints and allowed ports (ingress/egress) by service/component
- Expected IP ranges (CIDR) and whether customers must provide peering CIDRs
- VPC peering / PrivateLink options and the fallback behavior if a peering session drops
- KMS key locality for customer-managed keys and rotation cadence
- Data egress controls and how cross-border telemetry is handled
- Minimum ACLs for a hardened onboarding baseline

We'd prefer a short spreadsheet plus a one-page narrative summary and any diagrams you can share. We also need the SOC 2 summary page that points to controls relevant to network segmentation, and a diagram of the KMS keyflow if available.

Can you get this to us by EOD Tuesday APAC (your timezone)? We have a compliance review next Wednesday.

Appreciate it — please let me know if any of the bullets are ambiguous.

Thanks,
Nina Rao
Information Security Engineer
Medicore Health

2) For KMS: do you need evidence of our SOC 2 control mapping (just the control IDs), or the underlying Key Management procedure document as well?

Plan: I will assemble an interface matrix (spreadsheet) and a one-page narrative. Kim (cc'd) will pull the SOC 2 summary snippets. Marissa will help with the APAC peering behavior language and the diagram.

Target delivery: we can hit EOD Tuesday APAC as requested — I’ll send a Drive link with the matrix and a short PDF summary. If anything changes I’ll flag it earlier.

Best,

Hi Nina — sorry for the slight delay; attaching the packet we discussed. Below is a short summary and next steps.

Attachments:
- private_hosting_interface_matrix.xlsx (Spreadsheet, 58KB) — per-component endpoints, ports, recommended CIDRs, and required ACLs.
- soc2_summary.pdf (PDF, 120KB) — high-level mapping to controls relevant to segmentation, key management, and logging.
- kms_keyflow.png (PNG, 48KB) — simplified keyflow for customer-managed CMKs in APAC.

Key notes (short):
- IPs/CIDRs: The spreadsheet shows the CIDR ranges used by our Dedicated pools and an example template for customer peer CIDRs. Customers control their own peering CIDRs; we recommend a /24 per peering to avoid overlap.
- Peering & failover: We support VPC peering and PrivateLink-style private endpoints. If a peering session drops we automatically route requests to the regional fallback (policy: prioritise lowest-latency compatible region). We include recommended health-check intervals in the matrix.
- KMS locality: For private deployments we support customer-managed keys provisioned in the target APAC region. The keyflow diagram shows envelope encryption: customer CMK in APAC -> service data keys -> ephemeral session keys. Rotation cadence is customer-controlled; we recommend 90 days for high-sensitivity workloads.
- Minimum ACLs: The spreadsheet includes a baseline hardened ACL set (deny-by-default, allow only listed endpoints/ports).

Next steps for Medicore: please confirm the peer CIDR you will allocate and the primary bastion IP for initial onboarding. Once we receive that we can schedule a 30-minute onboarding call to test peering and validate routing.

Drive packet (read-only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c_redwood_med_packet

If you'd like, we can also provide an export in PPTX with the diagram for your compliance folder.
